rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers are prohibited from inquiring about criminal history, indicating that persons with criminal backgrounds will not be considered, refusing to rent or terminate tenancy based on criminal history, requiring disclosure or authorization for release of criminal history, demanding higher security deposits or rental amounts based on criminal history, refusing to allow addition of immediate family members based on criminal history, disqualifying tenants from rental assistance programs based on criminal history, or treating applicants or tenants differently based on criminal history. Landlords must provide written notice and opportunity to respond if taking any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history.
rules.citation: BMC 13.106; Berkeley Rent Board ordinance passed April 14, 2020
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.coverage_conditions: Legal city is Berkeley; applies to all rental housing providers in the city offering residential units for rent
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; Public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); Owner-occupied properties with 1-3 units where owner of record resides as primary residence; Units under rental agreement allowing owner move-back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; Units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
rules.sanctions: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief

On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106).

Any landlord found to be in violation of the Ordinance shall be subject to administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
